data.text: The Observer pattern defines a one-to-many dependency. When one object changes state, all dependents are notified automatically.

data.title: Observer in JavaScript

data.text: An observer has a subject that keeps a list of listeners and notifies them when its state changes. Subscribers register with `subscribe` and receive an unsubscribe function. This is the mechanism behind DOM events, RxJS, and every state store that lets components react to changes.

data.title: A minimal observable store

data.text: RxJS turns the observer pattern into a toolkit: observables emit over time, operators such as `map`, `filter`, `debounceTime`, and `switchMap` transform streams, and subscriptions are cancelled so resources are released. `switchMap` is what cancels a stale search when a new query arrives.

data.title: A debounced search with RxJS
Interview angle: forget to unsubscribe and you leak
data.text: Every subscription holds a reference to its listener, so a subject that outlives its subscribers keeps them alive and causes leaks and updates to unmounted components. The patterns to name are returning an unsubscribe function, using `takeUntil`, or tying the subscription to a component’s lifetime. That is the practical difference between knowing the pattern and using it safely.
